plates; page 1 contains planches X 41 and X 42

primary_facsimile_result.work: Sylvie Cauville, Le temple de Dendara X. Les chapelles osiriennes, IFAO, 1997

semantic_crosscheck.source: EPHE, Annuaire de la Section des sciences religieuses, discussion of Mendes in the Dendera Osirian chapels
semantic_crosscheck.statement: Banebdjed in the canopic procession brings the Osirian relics identified as the spine/backbone and phallus, explicitly cited to Dendara X 89, 7-10 and pl. 42.

critical_provenance_firewall: CG53469 at Tell Ibn es-Salam must not be directly paired with the Tell el-Rub'a djed without passport/coordinate evidence.
Dendera names spine/back + phallus; it does not itself name a djed as the relic pair.
DJED_AS_SPINE_PROXY remains a secondary theological/symbolic bridge, not a primary Dendara X 89 statement.

anti_cherry_picking.reason: The 42-nome procession contains duplicated and non-unique body-member assignments; a Mendes match cannot be promoted from a single row alone.
anti_cherry_picking.next_required_global_step: Complete row-by-row primary facsimile audit for all 42 administrative rows, commit v1.0 prediction table SHA, then open the held-out archaeological comparison exactly as preregistered.

canonical_conclusion: The IFAO facsimile removes the source-location uncertainty for the Mendes row: Dendara X p.89 explicitly locates the 'Bélier du nome mendésien' on the south-west wall and binds it to pl.42; independent scholarship identifies the cited lines 7-10 as the spine/backbone + phallus relic pair. This materially strengthens the textual side. It does not yet prove that CG53469 and any specific gold djed were a paired archaeological bundle, and it does not unlock the global 42-row confirmatory archaeology until the full primary audit is frozen.
